name: Germany
traditionNote: The archetypal codified civil-law system: the BGB, StGB, HGB and their siblings are the starting point, decisions of the federal supreme courts bind only the case they decide, and the Bundesverfassungsgericht is the exception — its rulings bind all organs of state and some carry the force of statute.
summary: A federal statute (Gesetz) is passed by the Bundestag, put to the Bundesrat — which must consent to some categories and can only object to the rest — countersigned, signed by the Federal President and promulgated in the Bundesgesetzblatt. It enters into force on the date it names, and failing that on the fourteenth day after the issue of the Bundesgesetzblatt in which it appeared. Statutory instruments (Rechtsverordnung) are made by the Federal Government, a federal minister or a Land government only under an authorisation in a statute that specifies its content, purpose and extent, and are published in the same gazette. Since 1 January 2023 the Bundesgesetzblatt has been published electronically on the Verkündungsplattform des Bundes, where the PDF carries a verifiable seal and the printed edition no longer exists. Germany is a federation: the Länder hold the legislative competence not assigned to the Bund, run their own gazettes, and administer most federal law themselves — so a complete answer to 'where is this rule published' often ends in a Land gazette rather than in Berlin.
hierarchy: Grundgesetz (Basic Law, 1949), with the eternity clause in Article 79(3) placing human dignity, the federal structure and the democratic and social principles beyond amendment
EU law (directly applicable regulations; directives implemented by German statutes) — applied with primacy, subject to the Bundesverfassungsgericht's reserved identity and ultra vires review
Bundesgesetz — federal statutes, and general rules of international law, which under Article 25 take precedence over statutes
Rechtsverordnung des Bundes — federal statutory instruments made under a specific statutory authorisation
Landesverfassung und Landesgesetz — Land constitutions and statutes, within the competences left to the Länder
Rechtsverordnungen und Satzungen der Länder, Gemeinden und Körperschaften — Land instruments and the by-laws of municipalities and public corporations
Verwaltungsvorschriften — administrative rules, which bind the administration internally and not the citizen

gazette.name: Bundesgesetzblatt
gazette.authority: Bundesministerium der Justiz (Federal Ministry of Justice), on the Verkündungsplattform des Bundes
gazette.coverage: Part I for federal statutes and instruments and Part II for treaties and international agreements; electronic publication as the official form since 1 January 2023, with everything before that in the pre-2023 archive on the same platform
gazette.desc: The gazette in which a federal statute is promulgated and thereby becomes law. The platform serves the official version as a sealed PDF — the seal, not the paper, is now what makes it authentic — and adds the Fundstellennachweise, the classified indexes of federal law (FNA) and of treaties (FNB) that German citation practice is built on.
gazette.howto: Search from 'Recherche', or address an item directly: the URL pattern recht.bund.de/bgbl/1/2026/237/VO.html is part, year and item number. 'Siegelprüfung' verifies the seal on a downloaded PDF, 'Verzeichnis der Sachgebiete' lists the subject areas, and 'Datenabruf' documents machine retrieval. Anything published before 2023 is under 'Archiv vor 2023'.
gazette.note: Citation is by part, year and page or item — BGBl. I S. 2745 in the old style, BGBl. 2023 I Nr. 237 in the new. Both forms are current in older documents, which is why the archive matters.

constitution.name: Grundgesetz
constitution.en: Basic Law for the Federal Republic of Germany
constitution.authority: Bundesministerium der Justiz and Bundesamt für Justiz; consolidated by the Dokumentationsstelle of the Bundesamt für Justiz
constitution.coverage: In force since 23 May 1949, amended more than sixty times; the consolidated text is maintained continuously
constitution.desc: Called a Basic Law rather than a constitution because it was framed as provisional in 1949, and left under that name after reunification. Article 79(3) makes the core of it unamendable, Article 1(3) binds all three branches directly to the basic rights, and the Bundesverfassungsgericht enforces both against the legislature.
constitution.howto: Read it article by article from the table of contents, or take the whole text as HTML, PDF or XML from the links at the top of the page. An English translation is in the Translations list on the same site.
constitution.note: The page is headed 'nichtamtliches Inhaltsverzeichnis' — a non-official table of contents. The authentic wording of any amendment is the Bundesgesetzblatt item that made it.

sources.name: Gesetze im Internet
sources.authority: Bundesministerium der Justiz und für Verbraucherschutz with the Bundesamt für Justiz; consolidation by the Dokumentationsstelle of the Bundesamt für Justiz
sources.coverage: Nearly all federal statutes and statutory instruments in force, in their current wording, continuously consolidated
sources.desc: The text of German federal law that everyone actually reads, free and reusable in HTML, PDF and XML. Statutes are addressed by their abbreviation — /bgb/, /stgb/, /gg/ — which makes it the most linkable legal corpus in Europe.
sources.howto: Use 'Titelsuche' for a statute by name or abbreviation and 'Volltextsuche' for wording; 'Aktualitätendienst' lists what has changed recently, which is the quickest check that a text is current. Each norm offers a whole-text download in three formats; the 'Hinweise' page explains them.
sources.note: Explicitly non-official. It is a service of the ministry, not a gazette: for the binding wording, follow the amendment back to its Bundesgesetzblatt item.

sources.name: Translations (Gesetze im Internet)
sources.authority: Bundesministerium der Justiz, translations commissioned from professional translators
sources.coverage: Around a hundred and fifty statutes and instruments, weighted towards the codes and business-facing law; each translation states the amendment it is current to
sources.desc: The state's own English versions of the major German statutes — the Civil Code, the Criminal Code, the Commercial Code, the Code of Civil Procedure and much of the regulatory law that non-German lawyers meet.
sources.howto: Browse the alphabetical list and check the version note at the head of each translation before relying on it; some are current, some are years behind the German text they translate.
sources.note: Translations are unofficial and are labelled as such. Only the German wording in the Bundesgesetzblatt has legal force.

sources.name: Rechtsprechung im Internet
sources.authority: Bundesministerium der Justiz und für Verbraucherschutz with the Bundesamt für Justiz
sources.coverage: Selected decisions of the Bundesverfassungsgericht, the supreme federal courts and the Bundespatentgericht from 2010 onward, anonymised, generally unabridged and updated daily
sources.desc: The free federal case-law database. It is the one place that carries the Constitutional Court and all five supreme federal courts — civil and criminal, administrative, finance, labour and social — in a single search, with the texts released for reuse.
sources.howto: Use 'Entscheidungssuche' by court, date, case number or ECLI; the RSS notification service pushes new decisions. Decisions before 2010, and decisions of courts below federal level, are on the individual courts' sites and on the Justizportal.
sources.note: Selected, not complete, and only from 2010. The official reports — BVerfGE, BGHZ, BGHSt — remain the citable series for older law.

sources.name: Bundesverfassungsgericht
sources.coverage: Decisions of both senates and the chambers, with the official collection (BVerfGE) indexed separately; press releases and forthcoming decisions announced in advance
sources.desc: The court that made German constitutional law what it is. Its decisions bind every organ of state, and where it declares a statute void or interprets one to keep it constitutional, that ruling is published in the Bundesgesetzblatt and has the force of statute.
sources.howto: 'Entscheidung finden' is the decision search; 'Entscheidungen aus der amtlichen Sammlung' gives the official BVerfGE series, and 'Geplante Entscheidungen' announces what is coming. Case numbers read 2 BvR 1202/22 — senate, procedure type, running number and year — and the site also carries English translations of selected leading decisions.
sources.note: A constitutional complaint decided by a three-judge chamber without reasons decides that case only; the reasoned senate decisions are the ones that move the law.

sources.name: Bundesgerichtshof
sources.coverage: The court's own decision database, hearing lists and press releases; the official collections BGHZ and BGHSt are published separately
sources.desc: The supreme court for civil and criminal matters, and the model for the other four federal branches — the Bundesverwaltungsgericht, Bundesfinanzhof, Bundesarbeitsgericht and Bundessozialgericht, each of which runs an equivalent database of its own.
sources.howto: Search the decision database by case number, date or senate; a citation such as VIII ZR 100/25 names the senate in roman numerals. Where the branches disagree, the Gemeinsamer Senat der obersten Gerichtshöfe resolves it — a rare procedure worth knowing exists.
sources.note: The court's own database is fuller for recent years than the free federal collection; older decisions may exist only in the printed official reports.

sources.name: Bundesanzeiger
sources.authority: Published under statutory mandate by Bundesanzeiger Verlag on behalf of the Bundesministerium der Justiz
sources.coverage: Official notices, judicial and insolvency announcements, capital-market notices and company disclosures, current and archived
sources.desc: The second federal publication channel, for announcements rather than statutes: official notices of ministries and authorities, court and insolvency notices, and the financial statements German companies are required to disclose. A great deal of regulatory law is promulgated here rather than in the Bundesgesetzblatt.
sources.howto: Use the publication platform's search across notices, or the company register for disclosures; the sitemap gives the full table of contents of what the gazette carries.
sources.note: Not a source of statutes. Where a rule appears only here, that says something about its rank — and some announcements published here are nonetheless legally operative.

sources.name: Verwaltungsvorschriften im Internet
sources.authority: Bundesministerium des Innern, in a joint project with juris GmbH
sources.coverage: Current administrative rules of the highest federal authorities, maintained as living documents and updated by the ministries themselves
sources.desc: The layer below statutes and instruments: the general administrative rules by which ministries direct their own authorities. They do not bind the citizen directly, but they determine how a discretionary power will in fact be exercised, so they often answer the practical question.
sources.howto: Use 'Titelsuche' by name or 'Volltextsuche' by wording. Documents are updated in place rather than versioned, so print or archive what you rely on — the version you read may be gone tomorrow.
sources.note: Administrative rules bind the administration internally, not the public. A citizen can invoke them only indirectly, through equal treatment.

sources.name: DIP (Bundestag)
sources.coverage: Bundestag and Bundesrat printed papers, plenary minutes, procedures and their stages, from the first electoral term onward
sources.desc: The legislative-history system. A German bill leaves a trail of Drucksachen — the government draft with its explanatory memorandum, the committee's recommendation and report, the plenary record — and the committee report in particular is what courts read when a provision's purpose is disputed.
sources.howto: Search by procedure (Vorgang), document number or keyword and open the Vorgangsablauf to see every stage with its documents. The documented REST API at search.dip.bundestag.de serves the same material as JSON for scripted work.
sources.note: DIP is a JavaScript application and needs a browser; the API is the route for anything automated.

sources.name: Deutscher Bundestag
sources.coverage: Current legislative procedures, committee work, plenary agendas and records, and the research service's published papers
sources.desc: The parliament's own site, more readable than DIP for following something in progress. Its research service (Wissenschaftliche Dienste) publishes short legal analyses that are often the clearest free account of a contested point of German public law.
sources.howto: Follow a bill from 'Tagesordnung' and the legislative-procedures pages; the analyses of the Wissenschaftliche Dienste are published under 'Analysen und Gutachten'. For the document trail and older terms, switch to DIP.
sources.note: The Bundesrat's own site holds the second chamber's stage of the same bill; it is frequently unreachable from outside Germany.

sources.name: Bundes- und Landesrecht (Justizportal)
sources.native: Justizportal des Bundes und der Länder — Bundes- und Landesrecht
sources.en: Portal to federal and Land law
sources.authority: The federal and Land justice administrations jointly
sources.coverage: Links to the legislation and case-law services of the Bund and each of the sixteen Länder
sources.desc: The map of the German legal internet. Because each Land publishes its own law, there is no single database of Land legislation, and this portal is the state's own index of where each one lives.
sources.howto: Pick the Land, then follow into its legislation service. Naming varies — BAYERN.RECHT, RECHT.NRW.DE, Landesrecht BW — and so do the licences and the depth of consolidation.
sources.note: A directory, not a database: nothing is searchable across Länder from here.

sources.name: BAYERN.RECHT
sources.authority: Bayerische Staatskanzlei, operated with juris GmbH
sources.coverage: Around 2,400 Bavarian instruments — statutes, statutory instruments, administrative rules and treaties — together with some 26,000 court decisions of the Bavarian courts
sources.desc: One Land's service, shown here as the pattern the others follow: consolidated Land legislation with the case law of that Land's courts in the same search. Bavaria's is among the fullest, and it makes visible how much operative German law is Land law.
sources.howto: Filter the navigation by Vorschriften — Gesetze, Rechtsverordnungen, Verwaltungsvorschriften, Verträge — or by Gerichtsentscheidungen and the branch of jurisdiction. The Bavarian gazette itself, the Gesetz- und Verordnungsblatt, is published separately at verkuendung-bayern.de.
sources.note: Bavaria only. Every other Land has its own service, with its own coverage and its own conventions.

sources.name: Verkuendungsplattform Bayern
sources.coverage: Bayerisches Gesetz- und Verordnungsblatt and the ministerial gazette, electronic and authentic
sources.desc: A Land gazette, included because the federal Bundesgesetzblatt is only half the picture: Bavarian statutes and instruments acquire force here, not in Berlin, and each of the sixteen Länder has an equivalent platform.
sources.howto: Browse by year and issue or search by title; the electronic issue is the authentic one, as at federal level.
sources.note: Bavaria only. Find the corresponding platform for another Land through the Justizportal.

sources.name: EUR-Lex (deutsch)
sources.native: EUR-Lex — Das Recht der Europäischen Union
sources.authority: Amt für Veröffentlichungen der Europäischen Union (Publications Office of the European Union)
sources.coverage: EU treaties, legislation, consolidated texts, case law and national implementing measures, in German among the official languages
sources.desc: Gesetze im Internet carries no EU law, and a great deal of what applies in Germany — from data protection to customs to agricultural rules — is an EU regulation that needed no German statute at all.
sources.howto: Search by CELEX number or subject with the interface set to German; on a directive, the national implementing measures tab lists the German statutes notified for it. N-Lex, linked from Gesetze im Internet, searches the national databases of the member states in one form.
sources.note: The German language version of an EU act is authentic alongside the others; the Official Journal edition is the binding one.

sources.name: dejure.org
sources.authority: dejure.org Rechtsinformationssysteme GmbH, a private publisher
sources.coverage: Federal statutes section by section, each with links to the decisions citing it and to commentary; free to use
sources.desc: What German lawyers open when they want a provision and its case law together. It adds nothing to the text itself; what it adds is the cross-referencing that the official sites do not attempt.
sources.howto: Go straight to a provision — dejure.org/gesetze/BGB/242.html — and read the decisions listed underneath it. Follow through to the court's own text before citing anything.
sources.note: Private and unofficial. Its statute texts track Gesetze im Internet, which itself is not the authentic text.

sources.name: juris
sources.authority: juris GmbH, a private company founded on a federal project and part-owned by the Federal Republic
sources.coverage: Legislation, comprehensive case law including unreported decisions, commentaries, journals and administrative material
sources.desc: With beck-online, one of the two systems German practice runs on. juris also builds and operates several of the free state services — Gesetze im Internet, the administrative rules database and a number of Land portals — which is why the free and the paid sides look so alike.
sources.howto: Access requires a subscription or an institutional login. The free federal services cover the texts; what the subscription buys is completeness of case law and the commentary layer.
sources.note: Private and commercial, notwithstanding the federal shareholding. Nothing here is an official text.

findLaw.task: Find the current text of a federal statute
findLaw.steps: Open Gesetze im Internet and use 'Titelsuche' with the statute's abbreviation — BGB, StGB, VwVfG — then read the provision from the table of contents. Check 'Aktualitätendienst' if it matters whether a recent amendment is already incorporated.

findLaw.task: Read the statute exactly as promulgated
findLaw.steps: Take the BGBl. citation from the footnote at the head of the consolidated text and open that item on the Verkündungsplattform — part, year and number resolve directly in the URL. Verify the seal with 'Siegelprüfung' if the exact wording is contested; anything published before 2023 is in the archive section.

findLaw.task: Work out what an amendment changed
findLaw.steps: The consolidated text notes the amending statute against each provision. Open that statute in the Bundesgesetzblatt to read the amendment as enacted with its entry-into-force article, then find the bill in DIP for the committee report explaining why the wording was chosen.

findLaw.task: Find a decision of a federal court
findLaw.steps: Search Rechtsprechung im Internet by court, case number or ECLI for anything from 2010 onward across the Constitutional Court and the five supreme federal courts. For older or fuller coverage, use the individual court's own database — the BGH and the BVerfG both run one — and for the official series, cite BVerfGE, BGHZ or BGHSt.

findLaw.task: Find Land law rather than federal law
findLaw.steps: Identify the Land, then go through the Justizportal to that Land's legislation service — Bavaria's is BAYERN.RECHT — for the consolidated text, and to that Land's gazette platform for the promulgated version. There is no cross-Land search, so the Land has to be settled first.

findLaw.task: Find the rule that is not in a statute
findLaw.steps: If it is a Rechtsverordnung, it is in the Bundesgesetzblatt and in Gesetze im Internet like a statute. If it is an administrative rule, look in Verwaltungsvorschriften im Internet. If it is a notice or a technical announcement, look in the Bundesanzeiger.

findLaw.task: Read a German statute in English
findLaw.steps: Check the Translations list on Gesetze im Internet, which covers most of the codes and much business law, and read the version note at the head of the translation. Selected leading decisions of the Constitutional Court are also published in English on its own site. Neither has legal force.

subnational: Germany is a federation of sixteen Länder holding the legislative competence not assigned to the Bund by the Basic Law, and executing most federal law through their own administrations. Each Land has its own constitution, its own parliament, its own constitutional court in most cases, and its own gazette — the Gesetz- und Verordnungsblatt of that Land — in which its statutes and instruments are promulgated and acquire force. Each also runs its own consolidated legislation service, none of which is searchable from any other: BAYERN.RECHT for Bavaria, RECHT.NRW.DE for North Rhine-Westphalia, and fourteen further variations, indexed by the joint Justizportal. Below the Länder, municipalities and public corporations issue Satzungen — by-laws on local taxes, development plans, waste and public order — published in the municipality's own official sheet, and these are rarely in any central database at all. Land constitutional courts decide questions under their own Land constitution, and their case law does not appear in the federal collections.
caveats: Gesetze im Internet is a ministry service, not a gazette, and says so on every page it serves: for the wording that governs, follow the citation back to the Bundesgesetzblatt item. Since 2023 the authentic form of that item is a sealed electronic PDF, and the seal is checkable — a text copied out of a consolidated database is a convenience copy however official the site looks. The free federal case-law database is selective and starts at 2010; the courts' own databases and the printed official reports go further back and further down. English translations are unofficial, incomplete and sometimes years stale. Federal law is only part of the answer: Land statutes, Land instruments and municipal by-laws are published separately, sixteen times over, and municipal by-laws often only locally. Administrative rules bind the administration and not the citizen, and the database that holds them updates documents in place, without versions. Finally, juris and beck-online hold much that the free sites do not, and both are subscription products whose consolidated texts are editorial work.
